title: Foundations: Retrowave - The Complete Guide
summary: What Retrowave is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Retrowave songs: Synthpop replaced guitars with synthesizers: icy arpeggios, drum machines, and detached vocals about modern love. Depeche Mode, New Order, and the Human League made machines emotional.

History: Kraftwerk invented the tools; Gary Numan's Cars (1979) proved synths could top charts. The 1980s belonged to Depeche Mode, Eurythmics, and Pet Shop Boys.

How the songs work: Retrowave favors the keys of Am, Em, Dm, Cm. Common forms include Verse-chorus with instrumental synth breaks; Extended 12-inch dance mixes. Players should master arpeggiators driving the rhythm first, then drum-machine patterns: linndrum, 808, 909. Synths need no capo.

title: Blue Monday - Retrowave Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Blue Monday by New Order (1983).
body:
Blue Monday — New Order, 1983. The best-selling 12-inch single ever.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of Dm):
Dm | C | A# | C

This study chart uses the 'Darkwave i–VII–VI–VII' progression, the Retrowave workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus with instrumental synth breaks. Listen for detached, cool vocal delivery — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Retrowave pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let detached, cool vocal delivery. Synths need no capo. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
